# The Public Sphere and Its Critics

Habermas's foundational account of the bourgeois public sphere argues that
communicative rationality is constitutive of modern democratic legitimacy
[@habermas1962strukturwandel]. His account has been widely influential.

Mill's defence of individual freedom against social coercion remains a
touchstone of liberal political philosophy [@mill1859onliberty]. The harm
principle is the cornerstone of that argument.

Fraser's critique draws on Habermas's framework while challenging its
implicit exclusions [@fraser1990rethinking]. Her concept of subaltern
counterpublics has proved generative for subsequent scholarship.
